messages:
support-rita: customer reported intermittent 429s + huge latency spikes when calling Redwood from behind a NATed proxy. they say calls usually succeed for a few seconds then start getting 429s for same api key. billing shows burst usage charges from retries.

support-rita: repro summary from customer: curl with API key from a single NAT IP, rapid parallel requests (~40 concurrent), initial ~120 requests succeed, then ~80 requests get 429 over next minute. rotating the API key temporarily removes 429s for ~30s then it recurs. they supplied logs.

support-rita: logs paste:
```
[2026-03-09T18:03:12Z] req_id=abc123 auth=key:proj-789 ip=34.120.56.78 latency_ms=95 status=200
[2026-03-09T18:03:12Z] req_id=abc124 auth=key:proj-789 ip=34.120.56.78 latency_ms=210 status=200
[2026-03-09T18:03:13Z] req_id=abc200 auth=key:proj-789 ip=34.120.56.78 latency_ms=150 status=429 quota_scope=org:321 used=120/120
[2026-03-09T18:03:14Z] req_id=abc201 auth=key:proj-789 ip=34.120.56.78 latency_ms=930 status=429 quota_scope=ip:34.120.56.78 used=95/100
```

support-rita: they also sent the request headers (redacted):
```
Authorization: Bearer sk-live-REDACTED
X-Forwarded-For: 34.120.56.78
User-Agent: app/1.2.3
```

kevin-eng: thanks rita. quick hypothesis: our scoping logic prefers API key/project attribution for per-project quotas, but we still maintain an IP-based fallback for NATs in case key-less traffic appears. the rotation behavior suggests the key-level quota is hit, then rotation causes a new key to be treated as a different entity (new quota bucket) until internal caches repopulate.

maya-sre: adding: we have a short-lived "auth-affinity" binding cached in edge proxies (TTL ~20s) that ties an IP to the last-seen auth projection to speed routing. when a rotated key appears, affinity flips and traffic briefly hits the new bucket — that matches their observed ~30s window. after affinity stabilizes, the org-level throttle (or IP quota) reasserts.

aj-product: customer is worried about cross-project leaks — could IP quota for a different org be throttling them? their logs show quota_scope=org:321 then ip:34... which is odd.

kevin-eng: possible. order of evaluation: 1) explicit API key/project quotas (if key present and valid) 2) org-level aggregated quotas (if project + key are within same org) 3) IP/NAT heuristics (when we can't attribute or as an enforcement backstop). but there are edge cases where both key and IP quotas are incremented for the same request during transition windows (race between attribution and enforcement).

maya-sre: the snippet showing both quota_scope tags means enforcement happened at two layers in different code paths. request A got charged against project, request B later got hit by an IP quota check — not the same atomically checked limit. that can make bursty clients see alternating quota errors.

support-rita: customer also reports they see a header X-Redwood-Quota-Bucket in responses sometimes with value "ip:34.120.56.78" and sometimes "proj-789". can we explain why it's flipping?

kevin-eng: that header is emitted by the enforcement layer that answered the request. if a proxy served from its local cache of attribution info, it'll tag with what it thought applied at enforcement time. when caches diverge during rapid key rotation + concurrency, different workers can have different attribution for ~TTL seconds.

maya-sre: repro suggestions: run a burst test from the NATed IP with a single key, capture responses including X-Redwood-Quota-Bucket and X-Request-Id, and correlate with the enforcement logs on our side. steps to ask customer: 
- run: for i in {1..200}; do curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code} %{size_download}\n" -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate &
- save the response headers (grep for X-Redwood-Quota-Bucket and X-RateLimit-Remaining)
- if 429s appear, do not rotate key until we tell you; instead capture a few minutes of traffic so we can correlate on our logs.

kevin-eng: quick mitigation for them: pin client to an explicit project-scoped key (not an org-shared key), reduce parallelism to below typical burst size (eg <20) and enable client-side exponential backoff to avoid billing spikes. we'll check if their Dedicated pool has per-IP safety caps that can be tuned.

aj-product: ops-bot FYI we should add a note to the runbook about how key rotation can temporarily evade/flip cached attribution and cause short-lived bursts. ticket created: #3421.

ops-bot: ticket #3421 created by aj-product: "auth-affinity cache flip causing alternating quota attribution for NATed clients" assigned to kevin-eng, priority=P2.

maya-sre: I'm going to pull enforcement traces for ip=34.120.56.78 between 2026-03-09T18:02:40Z and 2026-03-09T18:05:00Z. rita please ask customer to provide request-ids for any 200/429 pairs.

support-rita: will ask customer to run the non-rotating-key capture and send request-ids. asked them to pause key rotation. they say rotating is what made the problem go away briefly; they can refrain.

kevin-eng: follow-up notes: if we confirm race is the cause we can consider: - increase affinity propagation to 45s or - make attribution atomic (more expensive) - provide an opt-in header to force key-only enforcement for given projects. will estimate impact after we see traces. :thinking_face:

support-rita: customer ok with suggested mitigation and will provide traces tomorrow. marking this as an escalation. :white_check_mark:
